title: 内存优化全局方法论：观测、归因、干预、验证
key_conclusions: Memory optimization should run as a loop: observe, attribute, intervene, validate, then monitor.
Every conclusion needs a fixed scenario window and at least two agreeing evidence layers.
Build-time reductions such as R8 only count when device-side maps, meminfo, traces, and correctness checks agree.
A memory fix is incomplete unless rollback gates and user-visible side effects are defined.
shallow_points: The article provides a reusable worksheet but does not fill it with a real app trace.
It does not include quantified thresholds for every RAM class.
It does not automate evidence collection into a checked-in script.
It does not validate source paths against a specific Android branch.
discovered_connections: Day 72's build-to-runtime boundary becomes the validation stage of the global loop.
Day 68's cross-validation method maps directly to the evidence layering table.
Day 71's multi-process duplicate cost model becomes a rule to sum all package processes before claiming a win.
Day 74 should turn this method into a source-reading map across ART, AMS, lmkd, kernel, and mmd.
suggest_future_topics: Day 74 should focus on AOSP memory source reading paths and map runtime evidence to source files.
A future lab should check in an evidence collection script for meminfo, showmap, smaps, fd, PSI, vmstat, and zram.
A future appendix should provide RAM-class-specific acceptance and rollback thresholds.
A future case should fill the report template with a real low-end device trace.
knowledge_gaps: Need real before/after traces to demonstrate the worksheet end to end.
Need branch-specific validation for source file names, log fields, and tunable defaults.
Need measured rollback thresholds for CPU, I/O, startup, scrolling, and kill risk.
Need automation that aligns meminfo, Perfetto, heap dump, fd, memcg, and zram snapshots by timestamp.
applied_reflections: Applied Day 72's next-run instruction by focusing on observation, attribution, intervention, and validation.
Applied Day 72's build-to-runtime validation boundary by requiring device-side maps, meminfo, startup trace, and correctness evidence before accepting build-time memory claims.
Applied Day 68's cross-validation method and Day 71's multi-process accounting boundary in the evidence and attribution sections.
Applied the standing more-diagrams-less-prose feedback by using four Mermaid diagrams, compact matrices, command templates, and a report worksheet.
visible_changes: Added four Mermaid diagrams because of the more-diagrams-less-prose feedback: optimization loop, evidence layers, hypothesis scoring, and validation decision flow.
Added tables for stage outputs, evidence layers, Day 72 carry-forward, attribution buckets, hypothesis scoring, report template, and engineering conclusions.
Added command templates for meminfo, showmap, smaps_rollup, maps, fd, PSI, vmstat, zram, startup, and heap dump capture.
